doc_a.title: Epidemiological dynamics of airborne pathogen transmission across stratified contact networks [Study 1]
doc_a.abstract: In an urban population network, transmission of an infectious pathogen is concentrated among high-degree contact nodes. Targeted quarantine of hub individuals significantly reduces total infection velocity and attack rate across the community. Empirical data recorded over experimental evaluation cycle 1 verified these topological dynamics.

doc_b.title: Topological containment of self-propagating worm malware in software-defined network clusters [Investigation 1]
doc_b.abstract: In an enterprise router network, propagation of automated scanning malware is concentrated among high-centrality switch nodes. Dynamic isolation of hub routers significantly decreases infection velocity and compromise rate across the cluster. Simulation results recorded across test iterations 1 verified identical topological mechanics.

notes: Isomorphic epidemic spreading mechanism: high-centrality node isolation suppresses network-wide cascade.

doc_a.title: Monoclonal neutralizing antibody binding suppresses viral capsid cell penetration [Study 2]
doc_a.abstract: Following exposure to viral antigens, specific neutralizing antibodies bind surface envelope proteins, directly blocking viral cell entry and attenuating systemic intracellular replication. Empirical data recorded over experimental evaluation cycle 2 verified these topological dynamics.

doc_b.title: Adaptive stateful firewall filtering blocks malicious ingress exploit packets [Investigation 2]
doc_b.abstract: Following detection of hostile payload signatures, adaptive edge filters drop matching TCP streams at the boundary, directly preventing ingress buffer penetration and attenuating system compromise. Simulation results recorded across test iterations 2 verified identical topological mechanics.

notes: Isomorphic protective shielding mechanism: signature-targeted boundary blocking prevents internal infection.

doc_a.title: Negative feedback regulation of blood glucose concentration by pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion [Study 3]
doc_a.abstract: Elevation in systemic blood glucose triggers rapid release of insulin from pancreatic beta cells, stimulating cellular glucose uptake and restoring physiological glucose concentrations to baseline setpoints. Empirical data recorded over experimental evaluation cycle 3 verified these topological dynamics.

doc_b.title: Proportional-integral feedback damping of temperature deviations in industrial continuous reactors [Investigation 3]
doc_b.abstract: Elevation in reactor vessel temperature triggers rapid increase in coolant actuator valve opening, accelerating heat dissipation and restoring reactor chamber temperature to operational setpoints. Simulation results recorded across test iterations 3 verified identical topological mechanics.

notes: Isomorphic negative feedback homeostasis: deviation above setpoint triggers corrective proportional dissipation.

doc_a.title: Cyclic oscillatory equilibrium in coupled predator-prey population dynamics [Study 4]
doc_a.abstract: Proliferation of the prey population increases predatory foraging efficiency, driving an expansion in predator density that subsequently depresses prey abundance and maintains bounded cyclical equilibrium. Empirical data recorded over experimental evaluation cycle 4 verified these topological dynamics.

doc_b.title: Oscillatory liquidity dynamics between competing algorithmic liquidity makers and taker bots [Investigation 4]
doc_b.abstract: Proliferation of retail order flow volume increases predatory latency-arbitrage profitability, driving an influx of arbitrage bots that subsequently narrows bid-ask spreads and regulates order book liquidity. Simulation results recorded across test iterations 4 verified identical topological mechanics.

notes: Isomorphic Lotka-Volterra dynamics: resource boom drives exploitation influx, leading to cyclical stabilization.

doc_a.title: Long-term potentiation of repeatedly activated synaptic pathways in hippocampal circuits [Study 5]
doc_a.abstract: Repeated coincident pre-synaptic action potentials and post-synaptic depolarization strengthen synaptic efficacy, reducing action potential latency across frequently traversed neural circuits. Empirical data recorded over experimental evaluation cycle 5 verified these topological dynamics.

doc_b.title: Dynamic link-weight reinforcement along frequently traversed paths in ad-hoc wireless routing [Investigation 5]
doc_b.abstract: Repeated successful packet acknowledgments along selected multihop paths increase link confidence scores, reducing routing hop latency across frequently traversed network topologies. Simulation results recorded across test iterations 5 verified identical topological mechanics.

notes: Isomorphic Hebbian reinforcement: repeated successful transit strengthens connection conductance.
